{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |year=2017–18 |team=Western Carolina Catamounts |sport=Basketball |image=WCU Athletics wordmark.png |image_size=200 |conference=Southern Conference |division= |short_conf=SoCon |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=13–19 |conf_record=8–10 |head_coach=[[Larry Hunter]] |hc_year = 13th |asst_coach1=[[Anquell McCollum]] |asst_coach2=Brigham Waginger |asst_coach3=Wilie Freeman |asst_coach4= |stadium=[[Ramsey Center]] |champion= |tourney= |tourney_result= }} {{2017–18 Southern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2017–18 Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball team''' represented [[Western Carolina University]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Catamounts, led by 13th-year head coach [[Larry Hunter]], played their home games at the [[Ramsey Center]] in [[Cullowhee, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Southern Conference]] (SoCon). They finished the season 13–19, 8–10 in SoCon play, to finish in sixth place. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 Southern Conference men's basketball tournament|Southern Conference tournament]] to [[2017–18 Furman Paladins men's basketball team|Furman]].{{Cite news |date=March 4, 2018 |title=Western Carolina bounced out of Southern Conference tournament by Furman |url=https://www.citizen-times.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2018/03/04/western-carolina-bounced-out-southern-conference-tournament-furman/393012002 |access-date=July 8, 2024 |work=Citizen Times |language=en}} Following the loss to Furman, Larry Hunter resigned as head coach.{{Cite news |date=2018-03-04 |title=Western Carolina basketball coach Larry Hunter steps down |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/western-carolina-basketball-coach-larry-hunter-steps-down/2018/03/04/950a9056-1fe3-11e8-946c-9420060cb7bd_story.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180306142239/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/western-carolina-basketball-coach-larry-hunter-steps-down/2018/03/04/950a9056-1fe3-11e8-946c-9420060cb7bd_story.html |archive-date=2018-03-06 |access-date=2018-03-05 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286 |agency=Associated Press}} He finished his coaching career at Western Carolina with a record of 193–229 over 13 seasons. [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]] associate head coach [[Mark Prosser]], son of the late [[Skip Prosser]], was named Hunter's successor.{{cite news |last=McCormick |first=Bret |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Winthrop basketball assistant coach lands head job |url=https://www.heraldonline.com/latest-news/article206865969.html |accessdate=July 8, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Herald (Rock Hill)|Rock Hill Herald]] |location=[[Rock Hill, SC]]}} ==Previous season== The [[2016–17 Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball team|Catamounts]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 9–23, 4–14 in SoCon play, to finish in a tie for eighth place.
